Customization

To customize test scenarios below, modify the following fields
Notification Time: 11:47 AM local (2026-11-06T11:47:00-08:00)

Step 1: Get a Sandbox Key

Email your Voltus Account Manager or Project Engineer to get a Sandbox API key for use with sandbox.voltus.co. Use this key in place of YOUR_SANDBOX_API_KEY in the example curl requests below.

Step 2: Look at a Forecast

Anyone can read an example forecast from sandbox.voltus.co with the public API key secret, without creating a scenario: 
curl --request GET --url 'https://sandbox.voltus.co/2022-04-15/dispatch_forecasts' --header 'X-Voltus-API-Key: secret'
The response has one forecast series for each site and program: one interval per hour for the next 48 hours, each with a likelihood from 0 to 1. For how to use dispatch forecasts in your EMS, see the Voltus API documentation.

Step 3: Sandbox Forecast Scenarios

Each scenario below combines dispatch forecasts with dispatches. Create it with your sandbox key via the POST scenario endpoint, using the provided curl request. Then poll GET /dispatch_forecasts and GET /dispatches while the scenario plays out, and check that your EMS does what the scenario expects. How the forecast changes: A scenario holds a list of forecast updates, each with a published_time. GET /dispatch_forecasts returns, for each site and program, the latest update published by now. Hours an update doesn't cover read 0, and hours covered by a published dispatch in the same program read 1. Time is compressed: Forecast intervals are real hours, but updates are published 10 minutes apart (the Tick Interval above), so you see the forecast change within one sitting. Dispatches start on the hour, up to a few hours after you create the scenario. Passing the tests: You must monitor your systems to ensure they meet the expected result for each scenario. Voltus will not be able to monitor the output of your system. Tip: Scenario times are based on the Notification Time above. Set it to now right before you create a scenario. When you POST a scenario, the previous scenario is overwritten, so to restart a scenario, set the Notification Time to now and POST it again.
Description The likelihood of a dispatch in a two-hour block rises with each forecast update, then a dispatch covering the block is published. API Behavior: Forecast updates are published 10 minutes apart, with a likelihood of 0.2, then 0.5, then 0.8 for the block. 10 minutes after the last update, a dispatch for the block is published, and GET /dispatch_forecasts reads 1 for those hours.
Details 
- 11:47 AM: Forecast published for A Program (highest likelihood 0.2)  - 11:57 AM: Forecast published for A Program (highest likelihood 0.5)  - 12:07 PM: Forecast published for A Program (highest likelihood 0.8)  - 12:17 PM: Dispatch published for A Program  - 02:00 PM: Dispatch starts  - 04:00 PM: Dispatch ends
Each line is what one forecast update gives each hour. Once a dispatch is published, its shaded hours read 1. Expected Result Your EMS prepares for the block as the likelihood rises, for example by charging the battery. It discharges only once the dispatch appears in GET /dispatches, and only for the dispatch's start and end times. Creating the Test
